objective_authority: Lennon, 2026-10-19: "the transition gate must take the current policy and refuse when it differs from the policy the last launch reconciliation used." User audit scope; docs/architecture.md §§7,9,14,18; AGENTS.md.

requirements.statement: Both implementation authorization -> review and review -> verification refuse any declared ledger namespace unless a current policy is explicitly supplied and readable.
requirements.observation: Both coding edges reject omitted paths, nonexistent files, directories, empty/null/malformed documents, unknown fields, multiple documents, invalid versions and permissions. CLI refusals occur before the gate hook and preserve both record chains.

requirements.statement: Canonical policy digest must equal the latest launch reconciliation policy digest; field-order/whitespace changes may pass, semantic policy drift must fail.
requirements.observation: Both edges reject semantic drift. Canonical-equivalent JSON and permission-set order changes pass. Missing or wrong policy digest on the latest reconciliation fails even when an older digest matches.

requirements.statement: Reconciliation under the new policy restores eligibility only if all preexisting ledger/review/transition requirements also pass; merely presenting a changed policy must not restore eligibility.
requirements.observation: Clean new-policy reconciliation reopens the implementation gate. A dated policy observation followed by clean reconciliation reopens the review gate. An undated change with a prior launched review keeps the unauthorized-dispatch BLOCK. An old reconciliation snapshot and reconciliation without policy remain closed.

requirements.statement: No-ledger-namespace runs preserve existing behavior and do not acquire a policy requirement.
requirements.observation: No namespace returns before policy-file access. Omitted, absent and directory paths preserve legacy reconciliation-gate behavior. Existing no-namespace Gate B/C transition tests pass.

requirements.statement: Policy comparison and ledger gate execute under host run lock on the same snapshot used for transition append.
requirements.observation: CLI supplies the locked host history to the gate and holds that lock through transition.Apply. A waiting transition reads policy after lock acquisition. A real approved fixture transition appends exactly one record before a contending host operation acquires the lock.

requirements.statement: Preserve D1-D4 ledger freshness, integrity and namespace isolation plus Gate B approval binding and Gate C independent review.
requirements.observation: The existing suite and four permitted earlier auditor probes pass. Namespace enumeration, prior unauthorized findings, latest reconciliation, core-head binding and ledger inventory checks remain ahead of the new comparison. No scoped D1-D4, Gate B or Gate C regression was reproduced.

requirements.statement: Run full go test, go vet, go test -race and independent negative controls outside repository; inspect FAIL output even on zero exit status.
requirements.observation: Full normal and race suites, go vet, and 11 targeted top-level tests pass after correcting audit-environment/fixture errors. Both exit status and FAIL lines were checked. The deliberate removed-check overlay fails 22 refusal subcases.

requirements.statement: Verify repository status, binary diff digest and all untracked hashes unchanged; maintain blinding through frozen Phase 1.
requirements.observation: HEAD, branch, git status, binary diff digest, all Git-visible untracked file hashes and copied tracked bytes match the start freeze. No prohibited handoff or temporary audit context was semantically read. No unblinding was performed.

limitations: Isolation is context/blinding isolation in this fresh audit session. The filesystem and OS are shared. Repository read-only behavior is procedural; the sandbox technically permits repository writes. No original repository writes were performed.

The trusted host supplies the effective current policy path. This change does not discover an organization-wide policy or defend against a malicious host supplying an obsolete alternate file. A fully hostile host and unsynchronized external filesystem mutations are outside the stated threat model.

Outcome checks use local synthetic stores, fixtures and approval records. They do not constitute production execution or real human authorization. Some namespace enumeration checks deliberately use synthetic in-memory history to isolate the gate condition.

Scope is the six changed Go files plus necessary unchanged call paths. .serena/ and docs/handoffs/2026-10-16-arch-amendment-*.md are excluded. The modified docs/handoffs/2026-10-18-gate-d-d4.md was not read, including after Phase 1. All other /tmp/hma-gate-* and /tmp/claude-* context was avoided except the specifically permitted test file.

Audit-environment and audit-fixture failures are retained in E10. They are not implementation findings. GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false is required for nested builds in the Git-metadata-free source copy. GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR both point inside this output directory.

The current policy check covers host CLI transitions. transition.Apply remains a trusted lower-level API and does not read policy_path; this is explicit in its Input documentation and was not broadened by this change.
No approved Jev tool was exposed in the host tool inventory. Advisory judgments used the auditor/human fallback. No nested agent CLI, model API, subagent dispatch or optional unblinding was used.

Persisted test stdout/stderr logs are complete. Some console displays were truncated; the report relies on complete log artifacts, not those excerpts. Passing tests do not prove correctness for every possible input.

evidence.observation: Target frozen and requirements written before reading the scoped diff.
Six changed Go files inspected. Source copy includes 164 tracked files and no handoff documents.
11 top-level tests and 44 total test/subtest pass records. Includes original policy-drift probe and three D4 regression probes.
Same 11 top-level tests pass with the Go race detector. No FAIL line or race report.
Removing only the current-policy check causes all 22 policy-refusal matrix subcases to fail; current and equivalent-policy controls still pass. Expected negative-control failure.
Full go test -count=1 ./... passes in all 12 packages. No FAIL lines.
Full go test -race -count=1 ./... passes. No FAIL lines or race report.

evidence.source: vet-result.json; vet.log; version-result.json; version.log; environment.json; run_checks.py
evidence.observation: go vet ./... passes. Go reports go1.27.1 linux/amd64. Runner records argument vectors, cwd, environment overrides, times, exit codes and complete output log paths.

All freeze comparisons match. The full binary diff hash includes the handoff file that was not semantically inspected. Untracked hashes include the ignored-from-audit paths without semantic inspection.
